speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help assess your scalp and forehead rash, how long have you had these symptoms, and have you noticed any specific patterns like itching, pain, or fluid drainage?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Atopic Dermatitis (Eczema). The history of a chronic, scaly, red rash on a 36-weeker with a family history of atopy (father's psoriasis) and exacerbation in cold weather strongly points to eczema rather than psoriasis, which is less likely to present this way in an infant. I will recommend a skin scraping to rule out tinea capitis as a final confirmation.
